related_questions.question: Are PPP loans still being investigated?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, PPP (Paycheck Protection Program) loan investigations are still ongoing despite the program ending in 2021. Federal agencies, including the Department of Justice (DOJ) and the Small Business Administration (SBA), continue to actively pursue cases of PPP loan fraud.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, PPP (Paycheck Protection Program) loan investigations are still ongoing despite the program ending in 2021

text_blocks.snippet: Key points about ongoing PPP loan investigations:

list.title: Continued Scrutiny:
list.snippet: Even though the program has ended, investigations into potential fraud and misuse of PPP funds are ongoing.

list.title: Federal Agencies Involved:
list.snippet: The SBA Office of Inspector General (SBA-OIG), the DOJ, and other federal agencies are involved in these investigations.

list.title: Civil and Criminal Actions:
list.snippet: Investigations can lead to both civil and criminal charges against individuals and businesses.

list.title: Focus on Fraudulent Activity:
list.snippet: Investigations are focused on identifying and prosecuting those who illegally obtained or misused PPP funds.

list.title: Long Statute of Limitations:
list.snippet: Congress extended the statute of limitations for prosecuting PPP fraud to 10 years, indicating a long-term commitment to pursuing these cases.

list.title: Importance of Compliance:
list.snippet: Businesses that received PPP loans should ensure they have maintained proper documentation and followed the program's rules to avoid potential scrutiny.
